feature.label: Old Sevier
feature.title: Hi-Wire opens at noon on Black Friday with Mug Club memberships at half price, one day only

facts.label: When
facts.value: Fri Nov 27 · doors at noon, early · the deal runs all day

facts.label: Where
facts.value: Hi-Wire Brewing · 2020 Barber St, second floor

facts.label: The deal
facts.value: Mug Club membership $32.50 instead of $65 · 25% off to-go beer and merch, an extra 4 oz on every in-house pour, and the mug, for a year

facts.label: Thanksgiving
facts.value: Closed Thursday · back at noon Friday

facts.label: Weather
facts.value: Partly sunny and 51 Friday, 31 overnight · the decks are covered, the taproom is warm

body.text: Hi-Wire closes on Thanksgiving so its staff can eat with their families, and comes back Friday at noon, three hours early, for the one day a year it cuts the Mug Club in half. The brewery's membership normally runs $65. On Black Friday it is $32.50, and the brewery is plain about who it is for: people renewing, people who have been meaning to join, and people shopping for the beer drinker on their list.

A membership is good for a year. It takes 25 percent off to-go beer and the merch wall, adds four ounces to every pour you drink in the taproom, and comes with the privilege, in the brewery's words, of drinking out of a Mug Club mug. Once Black Friday is over the price goes back up, so the people who want it tend to be there early. The taproom is the whole second floor of the building on Barber Street, with the covered deck, the rooftop deck, pinball and foosball, and food ordered from Redbud Kitchen downstairs. Saturday the Vols are at Vanderbilt on the big screen; the weekend yoga classes are skipped for the holiday.

stories.label: Old Sevier
stories.title: The Pink Cactus gives away the first hour in its karaoke rooms on Thanksgiving night, the last free Thursday of November

facts.label: When
facts.value: Thu Nov 26 · the bar opens at 5 PM · the first hour in a room is free every Thursday in November

facts.label: Where
facts.value: The Pink Cactus · 1147 Sevier Ave · the private karaoke rooms upstairs, the bar and front-yard patio below

facts.label: How
facts.value: Rooms book online in one-hour blocks · 21 and up after 9 PM

facts.label: Weather
facts.value: Rain showers and 55, down to 35 · the rooms are indoors

body.text: The Pink Cactus has run the same Thursday deal all month: book one of the private karaoke rooms upstairs and the first hour is on the house. Thanksgiving is the last Thursday in November, so this is the final one, and the bar on Sevier Avenue opens at five that day as it does every Thursday. The rooms go in one-hour blocks through the bar's online booking, and the bar's own advice is to add a second hour, since one never feels like enough once the playlist gets going. Downstairs is the cocktail bar with Latin-inspired food and the big front yard; after nine the whole place is twenty-one and up. It is the one Old Sevier thing with a door open on Thursday night that has said so in its own words, and the rooms are indoors, which matters with showers in the forecast.

body.text: The night after Thanksgiving, the music venue at 808 Sevier Avenue gives its stage to an album release. Echo celebrates a new record with an early, all-ages show: doors at six, music at seven, and the venue's note that anyone under eighteen comes in with a parent or guardian. Tickets are five dollars before fees through the venue's page, the cheapest ticket on The 808's calendar this season, and the room is standing only. For anyone home for the holiday with a younger sibling in tow, it is the show on the weekend that lets everyone in. The venue's parking map is below for the lots and street spaces around the block.

facts.label: When
facts.value: Sat Nov 28 · 9 PM – 1 AM

facts.label: Where
facts.value: The 808 · 808 Sevier Ave

facts.label: Ages
facts.value: 18 and up · ID at the door

facts.label: Tickets
facts.value: $5 plus $3.71 in fees online · general admission, standing room

facts.value: The venue's map of the lots and street spaces around the block

body.text: The 808 bills Saturday as its premier emo night, and the venue said when it announced the date that it is the first one the room has held. The name is I'm Not Okay, a title anyone who owned a My Chemical Romance record will recognize, and the format is the one these nights run on everywhere: the songs from the middle 2000s that a certain age of South Knoxville knows every word to, played loud, from nine until one in the morning. It is eighteen and up with ID checked at the door, and tickets are five dollars before fees through the venue's page. The Vols finish at Vanderbilt around ten, so the room fills late. The venue's parking map is below.

stories.title: Small Business Saturday in Old Sevier: the grocery has filled its cases and the pottery gallery has the holiday show up

facts.label: When
facts.value: Sat Nov 28 · all day across the district

facts.label: Old Sevier Market
facts.value: 7 AM – 7 PM · 906 Sevier Ave, Unit 130

facts.label: Mighty Mud
facts.value: Gallery and shop 9 AM – 5 PM · 1528 Island Home Ave

facts.label: Weather
facts.value: Mostly sunny and 58

body.text: The Old Sevier District's November list puts Small Business Saturday across the whole neighborhood, and two of the shops have said what they are doing with it. Old Sevier Market, the grocery that opened on Sevier Avenue in October, keeps its seven-to-seven hours and has spent the month filling the cases: Joyce Farms turkeys, new fish, Whoa Doggie hot sauces, and the South Knoxville Elementary tote, thirty dollars with every cent to the school's PTO. Mighty Mud's gallery on Island Home Avenue is open nine to five with its current show of work by the studio's own potters, which is where the one-of-a-kind mug comes from. Sunny and 58 for the walk between them.

stories.label: Ijams Nature Center
stories.title: Opt Outside: a naturalist leads a family hike at Ijams Nature Center on Black Friday morning, ages six and up
stories.deck: Trail games instead of the mall.

facts.label: When
facts.value: Fri Nov 27 · 10 AM – noon

facts.label: Where
facts.value: Ijams Nature Center · 2915 Island Home Ave · check in at the Visitor Center for a free parking pass

facts.label: Cost
facts.value: $10 plus a 25-cent fee · register on the park's page · no walk-ins

facts.label: Ages
facts.value: 6 and up · up to 1.5 miles on rocks, roots and gravel, with stops

facts.label: Weather
facts.value: Partly sunny and 51 by noon, after a 31-degree start

body.text: Ijams Nature Center takes the day after Thanksgiving the way REI started taking it in 2015: outside, on purpose, instead of in a line. Friday from ten to noon a park naturalist walks families up to a mile and a half of trail, teaching the plants and animals that live in East Tennessee backyards through what the park calls observation and immersive trail games, which is to say the kids are looking for things. It is for ages six and up, ten dollars a person, and small enough that registration on the park's page is the only way in. Every participant signs the park's once-a-year risk form. The park's own post on it makes the case plainly: fresh air, fall color, birds, fungi, and, in its words, overall coolness. Dress for 31 at the start and low fifties by the end.

stories.label: Ijams Nature Center
stories.title: The season's last Fall Fungi ID walk at Ijams Nature Center goes out Friday afternoon, fourteen and up

facts.label: When
facts.value: Fri Nov 27 · 1 – 3 PM

facts.label: Where
facts.value: Ijams Nature Center · 2915 Island Home Ave · free parking pass at check-in

facts.label: Cost
facts.value: $15 plus a 38-cent fee · register on the park's page

facts.label: Ages
facts.value: 14 and up · up to 1.5 miles of uneven trail, with stops

body.text: After the Black Friday hike clears out, a different naturalist, the park calls them fun-guides, takes a smaller group into the woods for two hours of mushrooms and lichen. The workshop is the beginner's version: what a fungus actually is, the parts you look at to tell one from another, why the lichens on the quarry rock count, and what all of it is doing for the forest. Late November is a good time for it; the leaves are down, the logs are wet, and the bracket fungi and jelly fungi that show in cold weather are easy to find. It is the last date on this fall's calendar, fifteen dollars, fourteen and up, and registration is through the park's page.

stories.label: Ijams Nature Center
stories.title: Carve and Create: a beginner's block-printing class at Ijams Nature Center on Sunday morning, bring a shirt to print
stories.deck: One block, printed as many times as you like.

facts.label: When
facts.value: Sun Nov 29 · 10 AM – noon

facts.label: Where
facts.value: Ijams Nature Center · 2915 Island Home Ave

facts.label: Cost
facts.value: $18 plus a 45-cent fee, parking included · register on the park's page

facts.label: Ages
facts.value: 14 and up

facts.label: Bring
facts.value: Any tightly woven fabric you want to print: a T-shirt, a bandana, a tote · paper and all the carving and inking supplies are provided

body.text: Sunday morning's class at the park is the one that sends you home with a tool you can keep using. Each person designs a four-by-six-inch block, carves it, inks it in whatever colors they like, and hand-presses it onto paper or fabric. The park supplies the blocks, the gouges, the ink and the paper; what it asks you to bring is something out of your own closet, because the point of the class is that block printing is an easy and sustainable way, in the park's words, to breathe new life into old clothes. Smooth, tightly woven fabric prints best. It is eighteen dollars, fourteen and up, the parking fee is folded into the ticket, and registration is on the park's page. A second session runs December 20 for anyone whose Sunday is already spoken for.

facts.label: Thanksgiving Day

body.text: The regular season ends Saturday night in Nashville, which for the South Knoxville watch rooms means a seven o'clock kickoff and a late crowd. Earl's on Waterfront Drive runs its game-day board for it: two dollars off drafts, six-dollar Orange Bliss cocktails, six beer buckets for the price of five, two dollars off pizza, and four- and five-dollar shots, with the Saturday house margarita at eight dollars on top. The rest of the weekend is the rita calendar, a different one each day: ten-dollar Patrón mango on Thanksgiving, nine-dollar spicy pineapple Friday, and seven-dollar mimosas and Bloody Marys Sunday. The patio has been weatherized, in the restaurant's words, so the outdoor seats are in play all winter.

Printshop on Island Home Avenue takes a dollar off pints from half an hour before kickoff to the final whistle. Hi-Wire puts the game on the big screen on Barber Street. Puckers, the sports grill on Mimosa Avenue, says it will be open for every snap of the last regular-season game. For Thursday itself, know before you drive: Hi-Wire, Kern's and South Coast Pizza are closed for Thanksgiving, and SouthSide Garage's weekly list has no Thursday on it.
